title: Graphs and Breadth-First Search
summary: Modelling connections - vertices and edges, directed, undirected and weighted graphs, adjacency matrices, adjacency lists and edge lists with their costs, breadth-first search and why it finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs, rebuilding the path from parent links, connected components, two-colouring (bipartite graphs), grids as implicit graphs, and multi-source BFS.

cards.q: Why does BFS find shortest paths in an unweighted graph?
cards.a:
It reaches vertices in order of distance

The queue processes all vertices at distance d before any at distance d + 1, so the first visit is along a shortest path.

cards.q: A road network has 1,000,000 junctions and about 2,500,000 roads. Which representation?
cards.a:
adjacency lists

A matrix would need 10^12 entries; adjacency lists need memory proportional to V + E.

cards.q: When should BFS mark a vertex as visited?
cards.a:
When it is pushed onto the queue

Marking on push stops the same vertex being queued several times.
